agenda: Stage 1 (the pivot): transfer as a TRAINING-DIVERSITY property. Plus the review's missing counterfactual: equivariance-via-augmentation.

multi_family.runs: mt2_multi_seed{42,43,44}, gt_multi_seed{42,43,44}: dataset=drivaer_ml_surface + extra_datasets=[shift_suv_surface] (estate), frozen protocol
multi_family.instrument: drivaer 5-res sweep (in-family 1) + estate smoke (in-family 2) + fastback smoke (the HELD-OUT family: the transfer measurement)
multi_family.gates: D1: fastback zero-shot < 0.85 for MT2-multi on 3/3 seeds (single-family v3c/v4 sat at 0.87-1.07) -- the pivot's central prediction, p ~ 0.6; D2: GT-multi fastback vs its single-family 0.54-0.64 (does diversity help the incumbent too, or was it already saturated); D3: in-family drivaer held within 1.1x of each architecture's single-family level

rotation_augmentation.runs: gt_rotaug_seed{42,43} (augment=true: the z-rotation augmentation that has sat unused in the yaml), mt2_v3c_rotaug_seed42 (control: an equivariant model should be indifferent, a consistency check)
rotation_augmentation.gates: R1: gt_rotaug P1 rotation ratio vs GT's 26-32x -- augmentation is the classic alternative to exact equivariance and the review must price it; R2: gt_rotaug in-family cost vs 0.053 (orbit coverage is expected to cost capacity, p ~ 0.7 that cost > 15%); R3: mt2 control shifts < 5% on everything

v4_band.runs: mt2_v4_seed{45,46}: completes the best-cell 5-seed band for the review
